notes.title: New demo version - UI improvements
notes.content:
UI:
- Increased the color consistency in the game, so Blue always indicated "Primary" and yellow always indicates "Secondary". Resources, Power transfer, Power generation, Objectives
- Improved the settings tablet UI to clearly show the player you get extra setting value accuracy by moving the grabbed setting further away from the tablet.
- Added voice lines for Objective/Mission Failed/Succes.
- All available buildings have info UI in the staging area.


Gameplay :
- Builder tower now builds slightly faster when powered with primary power
- Builder tower more repair per projectile when powered with secondary power (player needs to manually force a collision between a damaged item and the builder projectiles)
- Radar tower increases radar range with primary power
- Radar tower increases vision range with secondary power

notes.title: New version of demo (0.1.40) - More UI
notes.content:
A lot of the changes in the new demo version are not visible, but hopefully the grabbing of objects is now even more reliable. 

Gameplay:
- The gun tower gets extra accuracy when receiving secondary power (Yellow). This used to be damage over time, but I doubt any player could see the effect. This is a better match because high (long range) gun tower stacks resulted in more missed projectiles, making them only good against groups of enemies. Now with the accuracy boost the higher gun towers remain deadly to single enemies. 

Visual updates:
- Terrain lighting has been changed to give more light on the shadow side of terrain.
- New VFX showing which towers are connected

UI :
- Resource color has been changed to Blue for primary and Yellow for secondary. This now matches the colors of the basic towers supplying this power. And it matches the UI elements (hover tower/resource node/locked shop items)
- In the staging area there are UI-elements of every tower and building on the table. Grabbing these will show some basic info about the object. Like what effect adding primary or secondary power has on them, and the amount of power they can provide. 

Other :
- VDXR should now also just work. (this was already in a hotfix, but I did not put it in an announcement)

notes.title: Bug fix : Unoffensible Demo now works with VDXR
notes.content: Someone reached out to inform me that the controllers did not show up when using VDXR. So the new Demo version fixes this issue.

notes.title: Demo now has spectator camera during missions
notes.content:
The final update before the steam wargame fest includes a spectator camera with some options to control it in the settings. When in a mission pick the cube from your arm and the settings will appear. On the second tab of the settings the spectator camera can be enabled and its follow properties set.
On the first settings tab the audio volume has now been split in music, SFX and UI. Reducing the UI and Music volume when recording with spectator camera could result in better clips. 

When new objectives are discovered during a mission there are now some audio and visual hints alerting you to this. So its easier to know when to check your arm for extra objectives.

notes.title: Music, Settings & Post Processing in the DEMO now!
notes.content:
The demo has been updated with 
- Music. It changes to more exciting songs when under attack. 
- To change the music Volume there is a 'setting tablet' you can activate from your arm. The tablet also has Render Scale and MSAA. 
- The game has been given a more cinematic look by using a postprocessing filter. 

- bug fix : Advanced tutorial secondary resource mining should now work as intended. 


Future
- more settings, and persistence between play sessions

notes.title: Demo 1.36 - New mining, building, and terrain damage visuals
notes.content:
- The amount of mining that is done is now always visible from the miner to the resource. 
- Placing and building a 'structure' now has some detail to make it less monotone.
- Terrain now takes visual damage from explosions, does not effect the gameplay. (performance remains the same)

The persistent terrain damage gives some sense of lasting impact from major battles. It also partially heals, so active battles can be distinguished from previous battles.

notes.title: Mission objectives and stacking power visualization included in DEMO
notes.content:
This update continues to bring more game data to the player, so decisions can be made more grounded in a real understanding of the game. 

1. This update to the demo gives the player easy access to mission objectives. They are now grabbable on the avatar arms. When grabbed a short summery of the objective is shown and the location of the objective is marked on the map. 
2. Current resources has been moved to the outside of the arm, giving the player an easy was to check resources. 
3. The stacking power of a turret is visualized even better.
4. All unique buildings now show their stacking power IN location and OUT location. Making it easy to know where to boost or extract power from. In combination with the stacking power visualization the buildings can boost defense or mining when in a pinch.

notes.title: New Demo version - Load/Save settings
notes.content:
A small update, this time. 

- Player scale,
- Waist height,
- MSAA,
- Custom controller offsets, 

are now loaded/ saved from/to file. 

This does not really add much to the game, but a bit of quality of life for players that play multiple sessions.

notes.title: Demo - terrain offset and player scale offset
notes.content:
Thanks to player feedback, it was brought to my attention the game was non playable when the steamVR playspace had a floor height offset. To fix this there is now a player calibration station. This station will allow you to set the terrain height and your default scale. 

This allowed the removal of the "move terrain up/down" tutorial step. And the terrain can now no longer be moved during a mission. 
The player scale is mainly so the avatar matches your size, it has no effect on the gameplay. 

These values are also saved and loading from disk between play sessions. They are saved when you fail/succeed a mission. To reduce amount of disk writes.

Today there was a short time where the build version was bugged due to the new changes. So a quick hotfix should have made the current version bug free again.

notes.title: Demo updated with more information : Resource, Shop and gunpower
notes.content:
The additions should all help to make it easier to understand the game without making the game easier. 

You can now see the income you are getting per resource on the UI element on your arm. This element will move over a shop item before you buy it, and it will show you the cost (the cost was already in previous versions).

Another UI element on your arm will now show you the 'Unlock power' needed to get extra shop items. The shop items will be shown in gray and while hovering over them the UI element will show missing power. 
The same element can be used to see the power available for a turret based on the stack of towers below the turret. This should make it easier to know what power is supplied by which base element. It also helps to see how complex structures have split their power to several turrets.

notes.title: Terrain shows you when you are under attack!! New demo version v0.1.31
notes.content:
A new version of the DEMO is now live on steam. The major change is that the terrain will now show
- tower range, radar range and combined vision range
- radar spawned, orange ring waves from enemy units
- red ring waves when your units are damaged

Never be surprised when you have suddenly lost your base, now you will be notified in time to stop it! 
I am really hoping this makes the game easier to play. Not knowing where the enemies were coming from, and losing units without even knowing about it was a big enemy of enjoyment. 

-The holotable also got a GPU performance uplift. 
-A bug the could lock a player in the AdvTutorial "Build a miner far away from the base" step has been fixed. 
- The second mission (desert) received a lot more extra units to help the player ease into the game. 

The 3rd mission is still very hard. I think this has to stay, since the real game will offer challenging missions to players. But in the real game this level of difficulty will only be at the final missions. 

Happy steam RTS fest next week, to everyone that loves this genre. 

Arnold

notes.title: Demo v0.1.30 - Simplify tutorial & blink tower stack
notes.content:
For most players the current update will be a bit 'meh', most of the changes are related to simplifying the first tutorial and missions. Until the advanced tutorial it will not be possible to use the scaling and rotating of the terrain. Snap turn on the joystick is still available, for players that are not able to turn around. 
This change automatically cuts the first tutorial in half, and hopefully will give new players a way to get into the real game a lot quicker. 

- Terrain offset change has been reverted to the 'two hand below terrain' movement system. This makes it much harder to accidentally move the terrain out of reach.  
- It is now possible to use the singlehanded movement system while holding something in your other hand. This is a big change to the gameplay options, but I think its not overpowered. 
- Losing an object from your grip without releasing the trigger, cannot directly transition to a movement input. So you first need to release your grip to 're-grab' the terrain or air.
- When a object is held, but is lost from the hand. The hand will not be used for movement until the grip is first released.
- When holding a tower block that is connected to other tower blocks, the entire affected collection is highlighted. 
- When taking damage your towers and buildings will blink. 

For the future I am afraid the terrain shader will need a big kick. Since its using a 3rd party shader currently there are some limits of what I can do with it. Both in adding features and in GPU performance. For the Quest 3 build I've already made a high performance version, but it came at a big cost to the visual  presentation.

notes.title: Release date moved due to next fest results
notes.content:
So for some of you there is a long history of getting the release date pushed further out. Let me just start by saying, I also don't like this. 

For me the core gameplay was ready a long time ago, but feedback from players and bad experiences from playtesters show that the game needs more work. And next fest has again shown that the game needs more work. Players don't play long enough to enjoy the game, they struggle to get through the tutorial. While I don't expect this game to be for everyone, the people who want to like it, should be able to play the game. 
So I will simplify and shorten the first tutorial by disabling scaling and rotating in the first missions. This should allow players to use the 'best' movement system for the initial impressions. 
There is also still a request for more transparent information, how much damage will a certain stack do? how much power is there in a stack? which towers are part of this stack?
Since I know all these things it is possible for me to enjoy the gameplay in its current state, but without this knowledge it is the player that needs to buildup this knowledge through losing a lot of games.... which is not a great way to learn. So I need to give more information to the player during the game. 

I still believe that this game is unique in VR, and once a player knows how to play it could give enjoyment and satisfaction. As long as the players don't play/enjoy the demo it makes no sense to expect the game to do well during release. 
So to those who have liked the demo in all stages of development, sorry the release is pushed back again. For those who are disappointed in the current state of the game, there are still things I can do to make it better.

notes.title: Demo update - Advanced buildings and resources tutorial - v0.1.28
notes.content:
At then end of the tutorial about resource gathering a section has been added about the secondary resource and how to mine it. The goes through all the steps:

- Unlocking extra build options by powering a factory with tower blocks.
- Gathering secondary resources using only primary resource structures. 
- Building at a distance from the base with a builder tower.
- Building Advanced Factory, which can build Missile towers.
- Using the missile towers to boost the mining of secondary resource. 

There is always a choice to be made in how you use your towers. Upgrading buildings, Mining resources, exploring or combat.

There was just a little time to push some small improvements to the demo before the start of next fest.

- The reinforcements in the first mission are changed from a single big drop to an infinite stream of smaller batches of extra units. To make sure you are never unable to do anything to stop the enemy.
- Added the ability to enable/disable MSAA, by pressing the M and N key  on the keyboard. This will at some point get a nicer version, but this was the fastest way to get it in. 
- Some small changes to the tutorial

notes.title: New Demo Page and Demo version for next fest
notes.content:
For next fest on Monday the demo has received a lot of improvements. There is a second tutorial explaining the resource mining and building construction in more detail. Splitting the amount of tutorial required before starting a real mission.

The resource cost of several buildings has been changed to make more sense. 

The first mission with mining and building (3rd real mission) has been made a lot easier to let the player have a chance of beating it. Its still quite a challenge. 

The shadows have been fixed, don't really know when they were lost... but with the extensive testing that was done more and more little issues where found and fixed. 

Super excited for next fest. Wish there was just a little more time to make the game even better, but it is in an acceptable state. 

With the new Demo store page its now also possible to leave a review of the demo, so another place where you can let me know your thoughts.

Good luck commander!

notes.title: Standalone Quest 3 Demo eating some PCVR development time
notes.content:
Last update was already a month ago, and the next update will take some more weeks. So I just want to let everyone know what's going on. 

The game has not been finding an audience on steam, and I don't think I can push it more into the PCVR direction (using more GPU and CPU to push out a better game). So I spend some time to go in the other direction and get the game running on a Quest 3. The demo with exactly the same gameplay but reduced visual quality is now available on AppLab. 
I never expected a RTS game like this would run on the quest 3, but with some sacrifices most of the gameplay can be left intact. 

This was most of the work from the last update. 

Now I am working on changing the 3rd mission of the demo to be a push mission. Where you don't wait for a timer to run out, but need to push to destroy the enemy base. I really want to make this mission the 'ultimate core gameplay demo mission' so when people like this mission they know they will like the full game. 
So far the missions all still had a tutorial feel, introducing a new building but not really challenging the player. The new version will be much more challenging, representing a mission half way through the campaign of the final game.

This will take some time, because I am changing the unit balance to be more challenging and reduce the amount of tricks a player can successfully use, to easily get a win. As an example the enemy now has anti-air towers with huge range to fire upon blocks that are thrown in their direction. All units have much higher HP, so its more common for your own units to take damage and need replacing. Single lines of enemies constantly running into your defensive wall are replaced by periodic bigger batches of enemies. 

I expect the steam demo will remain ahead of the quest 3 demo. But I will now consider if new features would also work on a standalone device.

notes.title: Unoffensible Demo Version 0.1.21
notes.content:
This is only a very small update. From feedback it was made clear to me that the hand interaction point was not clear enough. Players tried to grab things with their hands, the transparent controllers were not visible enough to signal you need to use them as a tool. So in this update the controllers have been made opaque .

While working on a standalone version for the quest 3 there was a lot of cutting in the shaders to find enough performance gain to make it run at an acceptable level. Profiling a lot also popped up some performance wasting code, so this is also fixed in the PC version. Although on PC the CPU is more of a problem than the GPU, so it would typically just pull through the issues.

notes.title: Tutorial cleanup and nerfing player scale
notes.content:
The latest version of the DEMO is focused on improving the first minutes of the game.

The tutorial now also has text explaining what to do. I was not a big fan of this, but having to repeat the instructions just to know what to do was excessive. 
Following in these footsteps the menu scene now also has text explaining what things do. For mission starting and selection these will only be shown for 1 mission, assuming the player will remember after using it once.

Mission select has been moved to the main table for easier access. Also an extra planet was added so there is always one within range.

The table height, postprocessing and renderscale settings have been removed from the menu scene. They only confused players at this time, and added little value.

With the tutorial there was little need for forcing the player to move some towers to get out of the cryopod. In removing this the amount of time it takes to get to the next mission is greatly reduced. 

------
NERF 

The HUGE player scale resulted in everything becoming very easy. One day the enemy will get anti air weapons to shoot down towers in mid air, or even attack towers in the player`s hands. Until that day the best nerf I could do is make the towers lose their turrets when they are moving above a certain speed. 
This helps because its no longer possible to explore the entire map by waving a tower in the air. And it also gives the enemy some time to kill a thrown tower before it can fight back. 
Towers hit by simple projectiles should not be moved enough to lose their turret.

notes.title: Demo movement system improved
notes.content:
After the full replacement of the movement system there were some small changes needed to further improve this system. 

- tutorial has now been updated to teach the new movement system
- translation speed improvement by drag and slide movement (this works together with the new movement system)
- Change terrain height during mission by doing a double hand lift/drop action
- Audio feedback for all move interactions

The current build still makes the player overpowered, and this will be addressed when the new movement system reaches its final form. Lets just enjoy it for now, even if it makes the demo too easy.

Next on the list is to 
- Switching missions needs to be better than with the Sun + planet system currently used
- Process feedback on the new movement system :-)
- Resource mining needs to be made more clear
- Still need to do a lot of audio effects where they are expected

notes.title: Demo v1.10 : New movement mechanic !!
notes.content:
The movement mechanic has been changed to a 'Grab air with two hands -> Scale/Rotate/Translate' movement mechanic. The teleport option can still be used as a backup or supplement.
In the hub-area/menu level the movement mechanic is still the same, but I'll probably replace that too in the future.

With this new movement mechanic there are a lot of new exploits in the game. I'll just accept this for now until I get more feedback on the new movement mechanic. Limiting the freedom of the player did not feel fun, so enjoy being overly overpowered for a few weeks :-). 

The choice for a new mechanic was between. 'Grab air' and 'teleport grenades'. This one was chosen because the overview when zooming out really gives the RTS feeling that was missing so far. 
Teleport grenades were an option because throwing is a core game feature. It would also allow the enemy to destroy the grenade before the player would teleport, resulting in being more confined to the area under your control. 

Known issue:
- the known terrain seems to be taken from the last vision of the previous mission.

notes.title: Sound, Streamer Camera, Dx12 and visible avatar
notes.content:
[b]Streamer options[/b]
This new version has a lot of updates for my own ease of use. It was mainly made to allow for a better trailer to be recorded. Including the player avatar. While the streaming controller is not really user friendly yet it can be found during the missions by raising your hand in the air. There are several settings related to a secondary camera and even a SBS mode.

[b]More Audio[/b]
An other big upgrade is the addition of many extra audio effects. Grabbing, releasing, building placement all give some audio feedback to the player. There is also a atmospheric wind to prevent complete silence. Projectiles will make a buzzing sound when they shoot past your head. 

[b]Better CPU 'stability'[/b]
The game will now run with Dx12, which used to crash all the time. So far it seems not to crash anymore... It does have the benefit of showing better performance in the steamVR 'Advanced frame timing' window. And it now seems to be possible to switch the framerate in steamVR without crashing the game. 

The main steam artwork for Unoffensible has also been updated, I hope this new version is more readable. It should also give more of a hint to what the game is about. Still not super happy with it, but I have to believe its good enough for now.

notes.title: next demo build delayed
notes.content:
Its been some time since the last new version was made available. This is caused by two things. The first one is that I've been working on the new trailer (which is currently in use). The second reason is that the current version of Unity has a bug that does not allow multiple missions to be played, so the game will crash as soon as you start a second mission. 

I expect the bug to be fixed in the next release, so I would rather wait for this than install an older version.    Normally I only upgrade when there is a feature that I need in the newer version. In this case I needed radars to be able to have different ranges, and the newest version did this automatically. 

The next demo version will feature 
- Opaque player avatar (Torso, Arms, Hands, Head)
- UI sound effects on every action the player does (during the mission)
- more sound effects Radar Ping, Miner Hum, BuildTower fire Thump.
- Radar range indicator shown when you don't have vision there.
- maybe some streaming settings I used to create the trailer. Currently the UI is not clear, but it does function if you know how... so maybe I'll disable it until its more finished

One of the streaming features is 3D recording in SBS mode, allowing viewers a 3D view of the battlefield. As seen in this video.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3iy60K-ELJo

notes.title: Demo V0.1.8 Performance improved
notes.content:
I hope you don't see the difference visually, but I've improved CPU performance. I should have focused on making the game more marketable, but I just wanted to do something fun. 

It all seems pretty hopeless, so shaving a millisecond from the CPU gives me some objective positive feedback from the game. 

Now back to marketing.

notes.title: Teleport movement, controller orientation and player avatar (Demo v0.1.7)
notes.content:
From player feedback it was clear the movement system was not great. While I was unable to fix this, there is now the option to use teleport + snap turn locomotion. This is mainly an accessibility feature, but until the normal movement system is improved, please use it to play the game.  

Controllers should now be correctly oriented automatically for Index, Quest 3, and Pico 4 users. These are the ones I tested, so some others might be correct too (expect Quest 2 to be equal to Quest 3). There is a Setting in the medical bay that allows the player to override the controller orientation for any  controller that is not correctly positioned automatically.  

Since the marketing is still a big issue, I wanted to update the trailer with a better visible player character. Resulting in the player now having a visible body. With arms and hands that should closely follow your real world arms/hands. 
It might be improved in the future, but I think it is good enough for now. 


The release date has also been pushed back again :-(. Really sorry about this, but as long as people are not playing the demo. It feels I need to focus more on marketing and working on the gameplay improvements takes a back seat (with the exception of useful feedback, which I always try to work on for the next version). With marketing work just getting added the timeline just shifts with this amount of work.

notes.title: Unoffensible SteamVR fest demo update
notes.content:
- Hands/controllers should now automatically be in the right orientation (tested on Index, Q3 airlink, Q3 steamLink)
- Tutorial and Mission dialogues are now skippable
- Reduced the amount of dialogue at the start of the game
- Tutorial, small changes to make it harder to do something wrong.
- Reduced frame latency in menu scene (solution did not seem to help in game)

Known issues:
- Removed the controller offset setting (did not work anymore with new system). Will try to return this later so any wrongly aligned controller can be fixed by the player.

notes.title: Bug fix for 3rd mission (missing terrain)
notes.content:
So the 3rd mission had an issue with the terrain not being visible, and a lot of extra units being there. I used this to create a new trailer, but forgot to put the level back in 'normal' mode. 

- The buttons on the controller in the 'start/menu-scene' will now rotate 90 degrees to indicate you are in "movement mode". This is just a temporary fix, I am working on updating the controllers, but that will take more time. 
- Also added the build version and VR controllers used to the local logging, so its easier to verify issues. The logging information is not automatically send, its only useful when people contact me with issues.

notes.title: Bug fix : Tutorial start stuttering + tutorial building not working
notes.content:
On some devices the start of the tutorial would 'hang' restarting the dialog a lot of times before proceeding. Followed by bought buildings not being build in the tutorial. This update should fix this issue.
Sorry to everyone affected, I test every build but not on all headsets. 

Other changes in this update 
- Movement :  In the 'Menu level' the wheelchair movement now has much less drag at high speed. Making it easier to travel large distances with reduced effort. Al low speed the drag is increased in order to come to a complete stop quickly. 

- CPU performance improvement : Physics settings in 'Menu level' have been reduced to save some CPU performance. Made possible by reducing the amount of sections in the wire. 

- Physics : Tower block interaction in 'Menu level' (stack in cryopod) should now be better.

notes.title: Small Update to the DEMO (V0.1.5)
notes.content:
Its just a very small update, to complete the previous tutorial update. The next version will take the more standard 3-4 weeks.

- Tutorial is now integrated in the voice lines/story
- You don't need to move before you learn how in the tutorial
- Scene transitions are now done with a fade to/from black, to minimise issues with loading times. (still not perfect, but good enough for now)
- The final accuracy/throwing test of the tutorial now returns missed towers closer to the target/edge. 
- Non-game/Menu scene Wheelchair now has bigger hitboxes, so different width people can move with more ease. (Not perfect yet, Movement is on my mind when looking at playtesters.)

notes.title: Demo now has a step by step tutorial (version 0.1.4)
notes.content:
A lot of people struggle with the unconventional movement and interaction system of this game. Although a tutorial is not something people want, it seems like the only option here. I tried to frame it into a realistic situation within the game world, and kept it very compact. Every time you restart the game, you need to complete the tutorial unless you have finished the first mission successfully. 
Originally the opening scenes and the first levels were ment to introduce the player to the gameplay by offering a lot of time and resources to figure it out, but I don't want you to suffer to find the right button to push. 

The next version will be in a smaller update and it will polish the tutorial and integrate it with the opening scene. It should not take too long, but it still felt good to add this tutorial asap.

notes.title: Big visual update on the Demo V0.1.3
notes.content:
Just uploaded a new version of the demo. With a huge graphics overhaul, with limited performance impact :
[list]
[*] high resolution terrain
[*] new textures
[*] more light in the dark missions
[*] fog (for more sense of depth)
[*] better colors on units, buildings and UI
[/list]

Also from player feedback:
[list]
[*] Guiding floor light to mission start button
[*] Disable 'reset brain button' on first run
[*] More visible Objective markers
[*] First level difficulty reduced
[*] Improved build building UI
[/list]

So please keep the feedback coming. 

Known issues:
[list]
[*] Sometimes the game crashes when a mission is completed (successfully or failed). Still trying to reproduce the exact cause of this.
[*] Sometimes the game crashes when resetting the brain. (Could not reproduce this)
[*] The physics of the cubes at the start of the game is a lot worse than the cubes in the missions.
[*] There is no way to skip a cutscene (annoying when replaying a level, trust me I know :-) )
[*] A lot of information is only in audio voice lines. 
[*] Minimum spec is CPU bound, this causes the game to run slower. This will be improved, but not in the sort term.
[*] Index controllers need to be reoriented in the medical bay.
[*] Game progress is saved only per finished mission. 
[*] If you restart the game all settings have been reset.
[/list]

notes.title: Visual overhaul incoming
notes.content:
So in response to the feedback, from the steam strategy fest periode, it was clear the visuals were not good enough for people to try the game. 
So I've been working hard on improving the graphics while not exhausting the hardware resources. However this does meen all the 4 levels need to be remade, the first level is done now and it should have been the bulk of the work. The other levels should take me about a week to remake. 

I hope you like this new look. Please keep the feedback coming, it really helps the game.

notes.title: Prosponed the launch date
notes.content:
So the steam strategy fest gave Unoffensible a lot more visibility. However this did not result in a significant uptick in visits. So something needs to improve before there could be a successful release.

Even though the entire steampage and marketing images were given an update right before strategy fest it was not good enough to draw in the minimum number of people needed. Almost no one played the demo, so even if the game was in a perfect state for production at this rate 0 players would know. I am left with no choice but to improve the game visuals and marketing material, so people dare to make the step to try the game. 

I am sorry for everyone that expected this game to release in November, but I greatly misjudged the appeal of the game in its current form. I like to play it, and I hoped that would be good enough. It will take months to redo the art direction and focus on marketing and playtesting. 

Please play the DEMO and leave your comments on the gameplay, the visuals will be improved to have a more satisfying astatic.

notes.title: Free Demo for steam strategy fest (VR only) & complete rework of the store page
notes.content:
With the steam strategy fest, what is a better time to announce a leap forward for Unoffensible. You can now experience the gameplay of the final game in an amazing ~1 hour demo. Having most of the features the real game will have it is a great way to find out what RTS can be in VR. 

The store page received a fresh layer of paint, with all new text, screenshots and trailer. And this is not all, the images used around steam for Unoffensible have all been professionally remade, to better capture the feel of the game. 

While the demo is a complete, playable, hour of making good choices there is still a lot of room for feedback from the community. So should features be added to the real game, they will also be added to the demo. 
So please let me know in the community hub if there is anything you liked/disliked about the Demo. 

Or even if you did not play the demo, please leave your thoughts on the community hub.

notes.title: Added cutscenes to the playtest and getting ready for Steam strategy fest
notes.content:
Just updated the free to try playtest to version 0.0.54. Before and after a mission there will be audio cutscenes (currently only in the first 2 missions). Also all the voice lines in the Menu level have been replaced by a more processional voice. 

Steam strategy fest is at the end of august, so the next cycle will focus on getting the cutscenes to also work on the remaining levels, and creating a demo version of the game from the playtest version. 

To increase visibility most of the time will be spent on redoing the steam store page, recreating the screenshots and trailer. Updating all the text and animated gifs. Maybe some light localization of the steam page. 

I really hope the strategy fest will get some more players excited about RTS in VR. Or at least get them to tell me they don't like the game :-). The game is definitely not done, but I feel the potential should be obvious. 

Whishlist, Follow, try the playtest its all free.

notes.title: Playtest V47 : Settings, Mission select and Story remade
notes.content:
There is a new version (47) of the Free Open Playtest. After months without a new version there is light at the end of the tunnel. 

When starting the game you will find yourself aboard a spaceship where a hovering droid will explain the situation you are in. This droid will also give you information about all the systems on the ship. You can move around on something resembling a standing wheelchair.

Currently you can 
- Change the controller orientation and offset
- Change the renderscale (FSR amount, affects GPU performance and visuals)
- Enable/Disable PostProcessing (affects GPU performance and visuals)

Just like in the older versions you can
- Change the table height, this is also the terrain floor height in game.
- Reset the game progress (start over)

What's next :
- The wheelchair movement will be incorporated into the fighting part of the game
- Some settings in the fighting part of the game will be made available
- The information from the droid will be improved in the menu part of the game


Known issues :
- The second mission is too hard. 
- Throw distance is generally too far. 
- Lasers don't have the right color.  

Roadmap:
- Improve level balance 
- Add very easy first level (defense only)
- Have a near 'final production' DEMO version ready for Strategy Fest 2023.

notes.title: Just a quick update, since there has been no new versions
notes.content:
So I am currently working on improving the game its starting room. The levels of the game are 'oke' at this point, and I know I can make everything work for the final release (It will just take time). But for the starting room the performance and gameplay are much less an issue. The room is mainly used to access the settings and get an overview of progression. 
The story will also play out mainly in this view. The level objectives will of course have rewards that make sense for the narrative, but the main plot will be made clear between the levels. There is more time and visual fidelity in this scene. 

It's still a work in progress, but the basics are under control. So here is a screenshot. The project is still in progress, but until I can add the entire new room there will not be a new version. Feedback on the current version is still appreciated on the community hub.

notes.title: Playtest still openly available (appreciate all feedback)
notes.content:
Please playtest the game and leave your comments. There are still a lot of people not playing this game (around 8 billion), if we could get this number down to 7 billion that would be great :-). 

The current state of the playtest version (v0.0.43) is very stable and will not change for a while (except for bug fixes and small tweaks). It will be used to recapture screenshots and update the trailer. Although its a playtest version there should be no bugs and there are 4 playable levels. The last level is not winnable but will give a highscore for how long you managed to stay alive. 

The coming weeks will be spend on upgrading the game engine version and all related packages. So this is the perfect time for feedback on the current state of the game. Because of reasons this upgrade will take longer than previous upgrades, but performance and visuals are likely to get a free bump. 
Since many changes to the code will be needed anyway this is the perfect time for me to change some of the uglier code to fit better to the current state of the game. 

Hope you have a nice end of 2022,
Arnold

notes.title: Pico 4 steaming works
notes.content:
The pico 4 has just been released and it looks like an affordable headset with good specs (similar to Quest 2). Before this week I was only able to test Unoffensible on the Valve Index. I tried to setup all other headsets in Unity in a similar way in the hope that it would just work. 
The pico 4 is the first time I tested this workflow, and I was pleasantly surprised the pico 4 worked right out of the box. 
All buttons are mapped to the right inputs, and the tracking is mostly correct (maybe I'll change the angle of the controllers a little bit in the game... the Index knuckles give a nicer experience at this time).

I don't think this type of game lends itself for standalone headsets, maybe with the next XR2+++ chip... or other more powerful chips become available. So streaming quality is definitely something I will keep my eye on during development. 

So if you have the pico 4, you can join the playtest and be sure it will work as expected. Here is a short video of my experience:

[previewyoutube=FVitOWZWUeM;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Deactivated the DEMO, please use the playtest to try the game.
notes.content:
So the demo was needed to participate in the SteamVR fest. It also adds some visibility from the free demo hub. But while many people have downloaded the demo, most have never played it.

It does not require a lot of work to keep the demo and playtest versions in sync, but still it takes a little. 

I think people expect a DEMO to be a small part of a completed game, and they use it when they are just not sure if the game is worth the money. Even with the default 2 hour refund periode, its safer to just play the demo and then decide to buy the game. 

The demo does have the benefit of only needing 1 click, and not the two clicks that the playtest needs. But the game is currently more in a playtest-y state. 

VR games look very different while in VR, compared to the trailer graphics. So I will reactivate the DEMO in the future when it can serve a purpose again.

Thanks for everyone who did play the demo.
